binding: The reader regenerates and validates the original case manifest, requires the actual energy deck to differ only by two EL PRINT/ELSE requests, verifies the expected FRD SHA-256, derives loaded work from that FRD/DAT rather than a caller-supplied number, and validates 16 contiguous Plate and 16 Web energy rows at the same time. Independent read-only review checked the raw deck difference, arithmetic, hashes and native block-diagonal operator.
decision: The torque-case domain energy allocations differ substantially, but equal resultant moments do not make the actions work-conjugate: S4 uses a two-force couple on deformable web nodes, while native B3 applies a moment to one rotational coordinate. The S4 web, B3 section and connection law also differ. This cannot isolate interface transfer or select A/B. A supported virtual side-work map or equivalent physically matched operator partition remains the specific obstruction.
limitations: ELSE partitions domain strain energy, not interface force, moment or virtual work.
The generic CLI records the DAT hash and closure ratio but does not independently require an expected DAT hash or enforce a closure threshold; this saved instance is bound by the verified record.
One mesh level does not establish convergence, stability or physical transfer accuracy.
The bounded external shell remains a different connection and section idealization from native L1.
Reported DAT and FRD precision produces nonzero half-work closure errors.
